note — the bold part is what the card te: The one who receives is in the dative: das Kind → dem Kind. The thing given stays accusative.
der and das both become dem in the dative.
die becomes der in the dative: der Frau.
Possessives take the dative endings of ein: meinem for der- and das-words.

English: She gives **her daughter** an ice cream.
note — the bold part is what the card te: die-words take -er: ihrer Tochter.
unser + em: unserem Hund.

English: You're buying **your sister** a present. (one friend)
note — the bold part is what the card te: deiner: dein + er for a die-word.

English: **Who** are you giving the book to? (one friend)
note — the bold part is what the card te: wer becomes wem in the dative: to whom.
The dative plural is den, and the noun adds -n: den Kindern.
Plural dative: seinen. Eltern already ends in -n, so nothing is added.
helfen takes the dative, not the accusative: dem Mann.
helfen changes e to i: er hilft.
der Nachbar adds -n in every case but the nominative: seinem Nachbarn.
helfen + dative: der Frau.
unser + er: unserer Nachbarin.
gefallen turns the sentence round: the dress pleases my mother. The person who likes it is in the dative.
gefallen changes a to ä: es gefällt. The thing liked is the subject.
The film is the subject, so gefällt; den Kindern is the dative.
gehören + dative: meinem Vater. No word for to.
gehören asks wem: to whom.
ein becomes einer for a die-word in the dative.
die Hose is one pair, singular in German: gehört.
ein becomes einem for das-words. Several shoes, so gehören.
danken takes the dative: der Lehrerin.
danken + dative: meiner.
der Gast → Gäste; in the dative plural, Gästen with -n.
schmecken: the food is the subject and tastes good to someone in the dative.
The verb first; deinem Vater in the dative, der Kuchen the subject.
dem Gast; nicht at the end.
kein takes the endings of ein: keinem Kind.
antworten takes the dative: dem Chef.

English: Why don't you answer **your colleague**? (one friend)
note — the bold part is what the card te: der Kollege adds -n outside the nominative: deinem Kollegen.
A stem in -t takes -est: du antwortest.
dem Kollegen: the -n of der Kollege again.
